messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT CREATED 1835002468 - P1 - Elevated 5xx rate and API latency spikes in us-east-1 affecting Hosted API and Dedicated pools.

alice_sre: seeing 5xx up ~18% across edge/ingress in us-east-1, median p95 latency doubled. Alerts triggered by rate_anomaly and api_5xx_surge. Began at ~09:12 UTC.

bob_oncall: oncall here, paging in progress. I'll grab the bridge. Who's got routing playbook?

carol_runtime: we have automatic region fallback but it's not fully engaging for dedicated pools due to ip-anchoring. Investigating.

dave_support: multiple customers reporting errors, some on Dedicated reserved pools. CS is triaging high value accounts and flagging impacted SLAs.

observability-bot: note: Datadog alert delivery is delayed ~2-3m; some dashboards may be stale. Logs still coming but slower.

alice_sre: created bridge: https://meet.redwood.com/bridge/1835002468

bob_oncall: aws-status-bot can you confirm if there's an AWS Regional issue for us-east-1?

aws-status-bot: AWS Health: us-east-1 EC2 networking API errors reported in us-east-1 starting 09:10 UTC. Official status: https://status.aws.amazon.com/incident/EC2/xxxxx

carol_runtime: confirmed root cause looks like control plane/API throttling in us-east-1 causing increased request fanout failures for our edge proxies -> origin. That explains simultaneous increase in tokenizing and model kernel retries.

alice_sre: mitigation plan (executing now): 1) enable region failover for hosted traffic to eu-west-1 2) scale Dedicated fallback nodes in eu-west-1 for affected customers 3) throttle non-critical routes (embeddings batch jobs, async ops) 4) open AWS support case and request escalation.

bob_oncall: executing step 1: updating routing policy.

bob_oncall: ```\ncurl -X POST https://console.redwood.ai/internal/routing/failover \\  -H 'Authorization: Bearer ${ADMIN_TOKEN}' \\  -d '{"from":"us-east-1","to":"eu-west-1","routes":["/v1/generate","/v1/chat"],"immediate":true}'\n``` 

carol_runtime: applying Dedicated pool rebind for impacted reserved pools: setting allow-failover=true on pool configs for pool-nd-*. Should cut over in ~45s.

dave_support: notifying top 10 impacted customers and offering status + workaround. Draft note: "We're actively failing traffic to eu-west-1 due to AWS regional control-plane issues. Expect brief reconnections; no data loss." Sending now.

evelyn_eng: observability note: because DD is delayed, also enable local sampling flush and forward critical traces to S3 for replay. Pushed temporary config.

bob_oncall: step 2 done: routing split now 70% eu-west-1, 30% us-east-1 (to preserve affinity). 5xx rate down to 6% from 18% within 2 mins. p95 latency improving.

alice_sre: step 3: throttling non-critical routes TTLs set to 0.5 RPS per token for embeddings and batch endpoints. Executed.

observability-bot: logs show errors: "EC2InstanceMetadataService::RequestTimeout" and "AuthProvider::TokenFetchFailed" for a subset of requests to the auth provider in us-east-1.

carol_runtime: that explains some upstream 401/502 combos — auth provider timeouts causing retries -> spikes. We're putting an auth-cache bypass/short-circuit for retries to reduce load.

bob_oncall: applied auth-cache short-circuit. Verified token fetches now hitting cache for 90% of requests.

dave_support: CS update: most customers report degraded but functional. Two customers on Dedicated reported higher error rates; offered immediate migration of their pool to eu-west-1, they accepted.

alice_sre: AWS case created and escalated to TAM. Case ID: 1234567890. Asked for ETA on control plane API recovery.

aws-status-bot: AWS update: engineers investigating EC2 networking API rate-limiting; no ETA. We'll post updates when available.

bob_oncall: handoff: I'm stepping out for lunch at 10:05 UTC. Oncall pass to evelyn_eng for next 45m.

alice_sre: acknowledged handoff. evelyn_eng you're the primary; pager duty notified. Summary pinned to thread.

evelyn_eng: taking over. Confirmed failover holding, 5xx now ~2.8%, p95 near baseline for eu-west-1 paths. Will monitor for 30m then consider rolling back.

carol_runtime: saved mitigation runbook steps to incident playbook section; added commands and required rollback steps.

dave_support: customer comms posted to status.redwood.ai with note referencing AWS incident and actions taken. Link: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/1835002468

alice_sre: postmortem TODOs: - triage auth provider retry behavior - make dedicated pool failover fully automated (without ip-anchoring) - add synthetic tests to detect control plane API throttles earlier

incident-bot: INCIDENT 1835002468 updated: mitigation in place, severity downgraded to P2, monitoring.

bob_oncall: :white_check_mark: good run, thanks team. I'll follow up on the AWS case and add timeline to the postmortem.

evelyn_eng: staying on watch for 30m. If AWS clears, we'll test gradual rollback to us-east-1 with canary traffic.

carol_runtime: note for postmortem: Observability latency due to third-party (Datadog) delayed alerts complicated initial detection — add alternative alert paths.

dave_support: closing customer urgent action items, creating CS followups for impacted accounts.

alice_sre: closing bridge in 30m if stable. Great job all.

incident-bot: INCIDENT 1835002468 - Bridge closed. Final note: Failover prevented broad outage; dedicated pool migrations successful. Root cause pending AWS analysis.
